prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Offshore wind farm operations and maintenance system supports safe, reliable generation, personnel safety, asset integrity, availability, and environmental protection. Boundary includes offshore assets, marine/shore facilities, personnel, participating organizations, cybersecurity, communications, fire protection, backup power; extends from turbine structures to Grid Interface Relay, excluding public grid beyond connection and unrelated port operations. Architecture separates offshore equipment, operational services, shore decision functions with defined interfaces.
Aliases: Glassfin = Turbine Controller; Morrowick = Offshore Substation; Pale Lantern = Weather Service; Juniper Vale = SCADA Gateway; Thistle Crown = Maintenance Planning Engine; Amber Quay = Shore Control Room.
Turbine Controller controls turbines locally and produces Pitch Deviation Notice; recipient unspecified. Turbine equipment: Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus. Blade Inspection Drone assesses blades. Offshore Substation collects/switches electricity; contains Main Transformer. Export Cable Monitor belongs to export system. SCADA Gateway controls offshore/shore supervisory exchanges and operational-information access; SCADA Engineer maintains interface configuration/integrity. Shore Control Room supports monitoring/coordination; Control Engineer assesses equipment/responds using operational picture. Duty Planner prepares/reviews maintenance through Maintenance Planning Engine, which organizes needs/resources/constraints without replacing planner judgment.
Weather Service supplies weather information; Metocean Buoy supplies observations. Marine Coordinator considers conditions/vessel availability; Fleet Dispatch Console supports dispatch coordination. Marine resources: Crew Transfer Vessel, Daughter Craft, Service Operations Vessel; Helideck supports helicopter access. North Access Scanner, South Access Scanner, Personnel Tracking Console support access/accountability/location. Warehouse System, Spares Hub support inventory/logistics. Work Permit Portal supports controlled-work authorization; Cybersecurity Gateway supports secure operations. External capabilities: grid dispatch, emergency response, communications, port support, suppliers.
Lifecycle: commissioning/acceptance requires documented handover/verification; routine operation requires validated status, approved procedures, current forecasts/grid instructions; maintenance considers condition/resources/access/production/fault severity; major refurbishment; decommissioning requires safe isolation/removal planning/residual-record transfer. Safety requires authorized work, hazard control, personnel/vessel accountability; environmental objectives require pollution prevention, minimized marine disturbance, prompt incident response.

Document units:
S071: The Cybersecurity Gateway provides a security boundary for connected operational services.
S072: The architecture assigns defined responsibilities to interfaces so that system changes can be assessed and managed.
S073: Operational personnel retain authority for decisions that require procedural, safety, or engineering judgment.
S074: This arrangement supports maintainable operations while keeping supervisory functions distinct from planning and human coordination.
S075: The operating organization combines shore-based planning, marine coordination, vessel crews, and technicians assigned to offshore work.
S076: The Duty Planner develops daily work priorities with input from the Field Supervisor and the Maintenance Planning Engine.
S077: The Marine Coordinator aligns vessel availability with crew readiness, port access, and the planned work locations.
S078: The Crew Transfer Vessel is identified in local procedures by the alias Kestrel Bay.
S079: The Vessel Master retains authority for navigation, vessel safety, and decisions about whether a transfer can proceed.
S080: The Fleet Dispatch Console is identified in local procedures by the alias Sable Orchard.
S081: The Fleet Dispatch Console gives the Marine Coordinator a shared view of vessel assignments, planned movements, and dispatch status.
S082: The Marine Coordinator uses that view to coordinate the Crew Transfer Vessel, the Service Operations Vessel, and the Daughter Craft as conditions require.
S083: The Weather Service produces the Squall Window Bulletin for operational awareness.
S084: The Weather Analyst reviews available forecasts and advises the Marine Coordinator on conditions that may affect marine operations.
S085: The Vessel Master evaluates local conditions before departure and continues to reassess them during the voyage.
S086: A Weather Hold pauses affected marine activity until the responsible personnel confirm that operations can resume safely.
S087: The Crew Transfer Vessel transports authorized personnel and routine tools between shore and offshore work locations.
S088: The Daughter Craft can support short-range transfers when the operating plan and conditions permit its use.
S089: The Service Operations Vessel provides a platform for work that needs longer offshore presence or broader onboard support.
S090: The Warehouse System is identified in local procedures by the alias Mosslight.
S091: The Warehouse System records stock status and supports preparation of equipment and consumables for scheduled work.
S092: The Storekeeper checks requested materials against available stock and coordinates replenishment with the Spares Hub.
S093: The Port Agent supports shore-side arrangements for vessel calls, crew access, and staged cargo.
S094: The Personnel Tracking Console helps the organization maintain an accurate view of personnel assigned to offshore activities.
